text:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert fired -> HIGH: gpu-memory-pressure-prod-gpu-1 (policy: gpu-oom-detect)

pagerduty: Incident #INC-2026-8422 created, triggered by metric threshold: gpu_mem_used_pct > 92% across pool prod-gpu-1

jamie: acked :hand: investigating. I’m picking this up as oncall.

omar: saw the alert. which pool? any customer-facing routes in that pool?

jamie: prod-gpu-1. routing table shows model-serving routes for chat-llama-x and redwood-embed-v2. traffic should fallback to prod-gpu-2 automatically but seems some requests are failing with 503.

alex: logs from the node show repeated CUDA_OOM and NVML failing to allocate: `CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY: failed to allocate 1.8GiB` plus `gpuctl: prefetch thrash detected`

jamie: copying log snip:```
[kernel] nvml: failed to allocate on device 0: out of memory
serving: error: cuda: out of memory at kvcache_alloc (kv_cache.cpp:142)
runtime: prefetch eviction loop high-frequency
```

omar: that smells like kvcache fragmentation + prefetch storm. Have we seen this pattern with recent release?

alex: we rolled a small LLModel runtime tweak earlier that changed prefetch window default (PR #3291). Could correlate.

jamie: immediate mitigations: 1) pause prefetch on prod-gpu-1, 2) scale up pool to add spare nodes, 3) reroute percentage traffic away from affected node. Doing step 1 now.

jamie: `/runbooks/gpu-oom -> step 1` executed: `kubectl patch ds gpu-prefetch -n infra -p '{"spec":{"template":{"metadata":{"annotations":{"prefetch.enabled":"false"}}}}}'`

omar: nice. also adding temporary taint to node to prevent new pods landing: `kubectl taint nodes node-gn0 gpu-oom=true:NoSchedule`

jamie: added taint to 3 affected nodes. scaling group autoscaler bumped from min 4 to 8 (requested). watching.

pagerduty: Note: Escalation policy advanced to SRE lead after ack not acknowledged by responder within 5m.

kim: @jamie @omar any customer impact? Support queue picked up 3 reports of 503s from customers using embeddings API.

lex: support triage: Customers A and B reported timeouts at 10:12 UTC, mostly short lived. No PII exposed. We're messaging both that we're investigating.

omar: ok, mitigation status: prefetch disabled, taints in place, autoscaler request in flight. Memory pressure dropping slowly from 94% -> 76% on the worst device. Kubectl logs show fewer `CUDA_ERROR` lines.

jamie: running targeted restarts on the serving pods on those nodes to reclaim fragmented GPU memory. Command: `kubectl rollout restart deployment/model-serving -n prod --field-selector spec.nodeName=node-gn0` (doing one node at a time)

alex: observed one pod restart recovered KV cache and freed 12GB on device 0. No immediate OOMs after restart.

kim: updating customer messages: "We've routed traffic away from affected nodes and applied a fix; requests may be slower for a short window. We'll follow up if any regression."

pagerduty: Automatic note: Incident state changed to acknowledged by jamie at 10:19 UTC

jamie: still seeing intermittent 503s on the embed route. I'm enabling model-fallback policy for embed requests to fallback to cpu-serve for small payloads to keep clients happy while we stabilize.

omar: can we flush KV cache before bringing nodes back to normal? idea: trigger `POST /admin/kvcache/compact` on runtime to reduce fragmentation.

alex: compact call executed on 3 nodes. compaction logs show reclaimed ~7GB average. Memory pressure now stable at ~60-65%.

jamie: removing taint on node-gn0 to allow pods back gradually. will keep prefetch disabled until PR reverted.

kim: support: customers no longer reporting new errors, one follow-up asking about SLA credit. we'll coordinate.

lex: file a short post-incident note for customers and internal ops. Tagging SRE lead for follow-up on whether the prefetch default should be rolled back.

omar: root cause hypothesis: prefetch window change + sustained high request concurrency on embeddings caused fragmentation and prefetch thrash leading to OOMs. Action items: 1) revert prefetch change (PR 3291) on canary, 2) add auto-compact after high-load events, 3) improve alerts to include kv cache fragmentation metric.

jamie: creating follow-up ticket: INC-2026-8422-POST with the above action items and owner assignments.

pagerduty: Incident #INC-2026-8422 status: mitigated -> monitoring.

jamie: handing back to oncall rotation notes: I’ll leave prefetch disabled on prod until morning. Omar please own the follow-up ticket for the revert. Posting handoff summary below.

jamie: Handoff summary: `Mitigations applied: prefetch disabled, node taints, node restarts, kvcache compaction, autoscaler bump, embed fallback to CPU. Customer impact: transient 503s for embeddings; support notified. Next steps: revert prefetch PR on canary -> roll forward with safe defaults, add compaction automation, improve fragmentation metric.`

omar: acked. I have the ticket and will action tomorrow.

jamie: thanks team. closing thread, will update if anything flares. :white_check_mark:
